references.text: Parallel text about the pig as an unclean animal because it has a split hoof but does not chew the cud, with the same prohibition against eating its meat or touching its carcass.
Detailed laws about uncleanness from touching dead unclean animals.
Prophetic condemnation of those who eat pork and other unclean food.
Judgment on those who eat pork and other unclean things.
Jesus permits unclean spirits to enter a herd of pigs, demonstrating the pig's unclean status in Jewish tradition.
Parallel account of the drowning herd of pigs, reflecting the pig's unclean status.
The prodigal son ends up feeding pigs, symbolizing the deepest degradation for a Jew.
Peter's vision about clean and unclean animals, which abolishes the Old Testament food laws for Christians.
